changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`

- names `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — the console object page. The inline branch becomes `ganttViewOptions`, the sibling of `calendarViewOptions` and `timelineViewOptions`: the declared block spread whole, title floored at `'name'`, no date field invented. - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the render branch AND the capability gate. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

### `.changeset/8114-detail-tab-activity-timeline.md`

- names `plugin-dashboard/README.md` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `README.md` ships in this package's `files`, so the example went out in every tarball. `DetailTabs` renders a tab's `content` through `ANGLE-BRACKETS(SchemaRenderer schema={toRenderableSchema(tab.content)} /)`, which makes `content.type` an SDUI node position judged by the component registry — so a reader copying the tab got the registry's `Unknown component type` panel (OBJUI-001) where the timeline should be. Same shape as the `line-chart` widget in `plugin-dashboard/README.md` (objectui#7896's census; fixed by objectui#7951) and the fourth known instance.

### `.changeset/8760-unfulfilled-chart-stubs.md`

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` — edited by this change

  > - **At render.** `SchemaRenderer`'s lazy branch re-checks `hasLazy(type)` on every pass and returns the `Loading ANGLE-BRACKETS(type)…` placeholder. `Registry.register()` deletes a lazy entry only for keys the loaded module actually registers, so for an unfulfilled key the entry SURVIVES the load and every later pass takes the same branch. Measured on `b775500af` through the real chain: `{ "type": "line-chart" }` painted `role="status"` / `data-lazy-loading="line-chart"` / `Loading line-chart…`, permanently. **Not** the `OBJUI-001` panel the card expected — no alert, no error, no console warning. A skeleton that never resolves reads to a user as a slow network. - **At authoring.** A stub is enough to put a key into `getKnownTypes()`, so `check:doc-types` and the CLI's generated `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` snapshot both blessed all three. `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` taught `"type": "line-chart"` inside a `card` body, and every gate was green on it.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1ccb5ba7d` (merge-base with origin/main): 12 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1870 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2482 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36801110380)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5c84eb4b5b51bd3dd966ff7ae37cde1fe51cb847`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#11295 (body, claim `5921983728`, dev report `5922666442`), PR #11303 (body, 14-file list, net diff `e3782d26ec..5c84eb4b5b`: +1218 / −36), the head's check-runs, objectui#11201 ruling B (`5921167691`), and objectstack `origin/main` `8d329f02ee` for `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` and `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` (both byte-identical to the dev's reading at `5f6b63a6fd`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **A1 — the dashboard signal is a host prop, `localized?: boolean` on the published `DashboardRenderer`: right.** Nothing on the served document can carry the answer: objectstack's `translateDashboard` returns the translated document only (`label`, `description`, `widgets`, `globalFilters` rebuilt; no marker). `MetadataProvider` is a type cache, and a provider-wide context would also cover the metadata-admin `DashboardPreview` and any inline block rendered under it. The prop is destructured out of the `...props` spread, so it never reaches the DOM. No string is compared with anything; the server's override rule is not copied. The docblock names the promise (the document arrived translated by `/meta`), the setter (`DashboardView`), the covered texts, the unset case (inline, preview, design surface) and the header-action exception. Clear.
- **A2 — which texts skip the bundle: right, measured against `translateDashboard`.** The server translates the dashboard `label` / `description`, per widget `title` / `description` and the sub-caption written into `options.description`; it does not touch `header.actions`. The diff skips the bundle for exactly that set (`tWidgetTitle`, `tWidgetDescription`, `useWidgetSubCaption(dashName, localized)`, the renderer's header `h2` / `p`) and leaves `tActionLabel` alone. An inline per-locale map is still collapsed: `resolveLabel(...)` and `pickLocalized(...)` run before the `localized` early return at every site.
- **A3 — the one setter is `DashboardView`: right.** Its `previewSchema` is the `/meta` read's document (`useMetadata().dashboards`, `preferLocal`) with widgets pruned by registered objects; the file's own comment records it was never a host-supplied preview channel. The other two hosts at the head, `metadata-admin/previews/DashboardPreview.tsx` and `DashboardWithConfig.tsx`, are design surfaces and correctly leave the prop unset. Observation, not a gap: `DashboardGridLayout` (`dashboard-grid`) still calls `useWidgetSubCaption(schema.name)` with no carrier; only inline SDUI blocks reach it today, so it belongs on the family list in ③, not in this card.
- **A4 — the view signal, `useServedViewItems` + `isServedView`, a per-view answer by identity: right, and the membership test is sound for every producer in the repo.** The hook reads `useMetadata().getItemsByType('view')` from `@object-ui/react`, the same context app-shell's `MetadataProvider` re-exports, so the test and the real console answer from one cache; outside a provider the read is the no-provider stand-in and every view keeps the bundle. A served view item lands in `objectDef.listViews` under the key `applyViewItem` stamps as its `name` (the registry's qualified `OBJECT.KEY`), and `buildViewTabs` makes that key the tab `id`, so `item.name === view.id` is the identity match. A per-view answer is required because one tab list merges three sources with different translation points (served items; the object document's own `listViews`; client-derived tabs). Name collisions: the test is name-only, not object-scoped; served names are registry-qualified while embedded keys are bare, so the only collision is an embedded key spelled as another item's full qualified name or as an aggregated container's bare object name — no producer in the repo does that. A later tightening (require `viewKind && object` on the matched item) is cheap and is noted, not required. Qualified vs bare: the tab list's ids are the merged keys, and the breadcrumb now resolves the URL segment with `resolveViewId` in both directions (A7), so the crumb and the tab ask the same identity.
- **A5 — "the server does not translate an object's embedded `listViews`": correct at objectstack `origin/main` `8d329f02ee`.** `translateObject` resolves `label` / `pluralLabel` / `description`, walks `fields` and inline `actions`, and spreads everything else through untouched — `listViews` is never read. `translateView` has no container or `listViews` walk, and `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS` is object, dashboard, view. The dev's further reading that nothing in the engine turns an object's `listViews` into view items is outside this review's named reads and is not re-read; the signal is sound in either world, because anything the engine did serve would be served under a qualified id and drawn as given.
- **A6 — scope beyond the card's named sites: inside the card's direction and the claim's surface.** The dashboard's own `label` / `description` (page header, renderer header, the AppHeader dashboard crumb) are the served document's title and description the direction names ("the renderer draws the served title and description as given"; `DashboardSchema` spells the title `label`), drawn from the same `/meta` document and re-translated by the same second pass. The record page's way-back label and the mobile switcher draw the tab's string through the one helper pair (`viewTabLabel` / `viewOriginLabel`), so the open view is named one way everywhere; splitting them would have left the old second pass on two of three sites. All of it sits in the claim's three named files plus one new hook module, which the claim allowed ("may need a prop or context the dev measures"). No file in `packages/layout`, nothing in `packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts`.
- **A7 — the breadcrumb matching the URL's view through `resolveViewId`: right and necessary.** At base the crumb indexed `listViews[viewName]` directly, so a bare `/view/in_progress` missed the qualified key and drew the humanized slug whatever was served (the measured `en` reading); the pin could not hold without it. The matcher is the one in `@object-ui/core` the object page opens views with; no second copy. Its result is a strict superset of the direct lookup (exact, bare-to-qualified, qualified-to-bare), so no previously matched view changes.
- **A8 — pins: the card's four are all present, through the real components, in `en` and `zh-CN`.** (i) served widget title carrying a published edit drawn as served: `DashboardRenderer.servedLocalized-11295` and `DashboardView.servedLocalized-11295`, both locales; (ii) an unedited widget still shows the packaged translation the server put in: present in all four files; (iii) the inline, non-served control keeps the bundle: the third block of the renderer pin; (iv) the view's tab and breadcrumb: `ObjectView.servedViewLabel-11295` (real `ViewTabBar`) and `AppHeader.servedLabels-11295` (bare and qualified URL, plus the dashboard crumb and a not-served-dashboard control). Cell count 6 + 4 + 6 + 10 = 26. Red-first 2 of 6 on the renderer pin is the predicted split (the two edited cells; unedited and inline green). The reverse of the five implementation files turning 12 of 26 red — 2 renderer, 2 page, 2 tab, 6 crumb (bare, qualified, dashboard, both locales) — with every unedited and control cell green is the split the cells imply; not re-run here, consistent with the test bodies. Not separately pinned: the mobile switcher and the way-back label, which draw through the same helpers as the pinned tab.
- **A9 — the card's three prohibitions hold.** No second translation pass over a served value on any touched site; no copy of the server's override rule (no `packagedBase` comparison, no string equality anywhere in the diff); `packages/layout` untouched (objectui#11201, seat 2).
- **A10 — gates at the head (check-runs are the verdict).** Concluded green: Lint, Type Check, Spec Main Shape Gate, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Test (dist pins), Test shards 2/8, 3/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, 8/8, Doc Snippet Type Check, README Export Check (the two the dev could not run locally), Changeset Bump Policy / Declaration / Claim Re-read / Fixed Group / Overwrite Report, Doc Fence / Example Id / Component Type / Internal Docs Link checks, Line Citation Gate, Control Byte Scan, Inert vi.mock Specifier Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Pre-Install Import Graph Check, Live E2E (informational), the skill checks, label, Action Ref Convention, Bundle Analysis, Docs Route Eager Closure Check. Skipped by path condition: the coverage shard, Test (coverage), dependabot. **Not concluded at this read: Test (shard 1/8) and Test (shard 4/8)** — named as in progress, treated as neither pass nor fail; the merge waits on their conclusion, not this record.
- **A11 — docs.** `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` document the prop in prose, no new fence; the doc gates above are green on the head.
- Observation, non-blocking, pre-existing class: the AppHeader dashboard crumb and `DashboardView`'s `resolveKeyedI18nLabel` hand a served `label` through without collapsing an inline locale map; the base did the same whenever the bundle missed, and `DashboardSchema.label` is not measured here to be map-valued.

### ② Semver level

- Two changesets, one per released package, `check-changeset-presence` and the Changeset gates green.
- `@object-ui/app-shell: patch` — right. No export changes; `hooks/useServedViewItems.ts` is an internal module; `DashboardView`, `ObjectView`, `AppHeader` change behaviour only.
- `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard: patch` — holds, with `minor` the stricter reading. The diff adds one public optional prop, `localized?: boolean`, to the exported `DashboardRenderer` (`DashboardRendererProps`, carried into `dist/DashboardRenderer.d.ts`), and an optional second parameter to `useWidgetSubCaption`, which the package barrel (`src/index.tsx`) does not export. Under semver proper an additive public prop is a `minor`; the repo's written policy (AGENTS.md 版本号策略) pins only `major` and leaves minor/patch to the normal bump, the changeset body names the new surface and its contract, and the fixed group takes the highest bump either way. Judged acceptable as a fix changeset whose vehicle is one additive optional prop; the seat may raise it to `minor` before merge — not blocking.
- `Clause-②: yes` — right. A published renderer's prop surface changes, which is the very case objectui#11201's ruling B separated out when it set `Clause-②: no` for a renderer change with "no schema, type or public prop change". The ACCEPT re-reads the export the dev named (`localized` in the rebuilt `.d.ts`).
